Oahe.
properties.instruction:

weather conditions.

shelter inside a building or vehicle.

to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Ferris Burn Scar in...
Northwestern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 745 AM MDT.

* At 542 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated several rounds of
thunderstorms producing moderate to heavy rainfall rates over the
Ferris Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen.
The expected rainfall rate is 0.7 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Ferris Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Ferris Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Areas in and near the Ferris burn scar of Northwestern Dolores
County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Ferris Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

jackets.

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Monday evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected through Tuesday evening.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna will likely reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

the next couple of days.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 13 at 1:21PM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, Fox and Chena Hot Springs Road From
Mp 12 To Mp 34.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. More rain is expected beginning
Tuesday and will continue through Wednesday afternoon. Storm
total rainfall during this time will be around 0.50" to 1.00". It
has been very wet lately and this amount of rain has the
potential to bring the Chena and Little Chena Rivers above minor
flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor the latest forecasts and be alert for possible
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 13 at 12:09PM AKDT until September 15 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk: Water levels as
high as 1.0 to 2.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 40 to 45 mph before
winds transition to west Tuesday morning, diminishing impacts.

Toksook Bay and Tununak: West winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
45 to 50 mph beginning Tuesday morning. Water levels as high as
0.5 to 1.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak, Kipnuk, Toksook Bay, and Tununak.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Monday to 10 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is potential for coastal erosion due to high
surf. The coastal flood threat is low to medium for
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk (30 to 40 percent). The
coastal flood threat is low (10 to 20 percent) for Toksook Bay
and Tununak.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A developing low pressure system will drive
a fetch of strong southwest winds towards the Kuskokwim Delta
Coast early Monday afternoon, which will result in increased
wave activity. Large breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet for the
Kuskokwim Delta coast will continue into Tuesday morning, which
will also coincide with high tide, enhancing coastal impacts.
Southwest winds shut off later Tuesday morning for the Kuskokwim
Delta Coast and attention then shifts to Toksook Bay and Tununak
as west winds take over and the low moves inland. Strong west
winds will bring in higher seas of 1 to 3 feet for Toksook Bay
and Tununak. Conditions are on track to improve as the low moves
farther inland Tuesday night. Additionally, periods of moderate
to heavy rainfall will precede the advisory duration.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect the
coastline in the advisory area, producing rip currents and
localized erosion.

* WHAT...Heat index values up to 109 expected.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southeast Texas.

* WHEN...For the Heat Advisory today, until 6 PM CDT this evening.
For the Heat Advisory Monday, from 11 AM to 6 PM CDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.
